scope: Post-0.2 headless architecture evaluation through Scenario 08

evidenceBoundary.note: Scenario-specific deterministic oracles and exact fixture SHAs are retained in the individual result records. This synthesis does not pretend heterogeneous scenario repetitions are one IID statistical sample.

evidence: Scenario 01 single-agent Luna missed malformed internal whitespace accepted by its own tests.
Scenario 03 single-agent executions missed the subtle stable-order contract in observed repetitions while reviewed executions passed.
Scenario 02 strong review found backwards-compatibility defects and drove successful remediation.
Scenario 06 strong review found missing requested regression coverage and drove successful same-implementer remediation.

persistentPlanningCoordinator.decision: remove from default cohesive-task path; activate conditionally
evidence: Across normal low/medium-risk scenarios the Luna->Terra reviewed route matched deterministic correctness while materially reducing AI-credit and usually call/token/latency cost versus released v0.2.
Scenario 06 is the important exception on raw calls/input: remediation made the lean route slightly larger there, yet it remained much cheaper in credits and faster while preserving correctness.
No completed cohesive-task benchmark has demonstrated unique semantic value from paying a planning coordinator before every task.
activateWhen: task requires nontrivial decomposition or architectural choice
cross-component scope cannot be represented as one cohesive acceptance boundary
recovery policy needs a strong coordinator after genuine BLOCKED evidence

workerBPeerConvergence.decision: remove from default low/medium-risk path; retain as high-risk escalation
workerBPeerConvergence.confidence: high that it is not default-cost-efficient; preliminary positive evidence for high-risk escalation
evidence: Peer topologies did not show a cost/correctness advantage on ordinary cohesive scenarios.

Scenario 08 produced the first direct unique-value event: GPT-5.4 mini Worker B found and fixed a real root-self path-containment defect in Luna Worker A's first security-boundary implementation before final Terra review.
The final peer run passed all six external security checks.
activateWhen: deterministic route/risk is high-risk, especially security, privilege, containment, destructive data, build/release integrity or cross-boundary behavior
task is broad enough that independent implementation context is likely to expose different assumptions

singleAgentModifyingPath.decision: do not use as general default
evidence: Its cost is lowest but observed correctness misses make it failure-adjusted unattractive for general modifying work.
Keep only for deliberately narrow/read-only/trivial routes with strong deterministic acceptance gates.

conditionalRecovery.decision: retain on demand after deterministic BLOCKED
evidence: Policy-correct Scenario 04 runs show Luna->Terra plus on-demand Terra recovery preserves the operator-prerequisite trajectory at far lower average cost than historical passing v0.2 recovery runs.
Synthetic credential and blocked-validation experiments show prerequisite integrity must be deterministic engine policy, not merely prompt guidance.

scenario08.interpretation: On final-oracle metrics Luna->Terra is cheapest. The peer route pays a significant assurance premium but demonstrated unique semantic defect detection. Released v0.2 is far more expensive in AI credits than either lean route and its always-on coordinator is not supported by this task.

paretoConclusion.normalTasks: Luna->Terra is the observed Pareto-leading default candidate: same deterministic correctness with much lower credit cost and usually lower calls/tokens/latency than v0.2.
paretoConclusion.highRiskTasks: There is an assurance/cost frontier rather than one winner: Luna->Terra is cheapest; Luna<->diversified peer->Terra buys demonstrable independent defect discovery at a bounded premium. Use risk to choose between them.
paretoConclusion.releasedV02: Keep as released stable reference until adaptive productization is implemented and validated; do not carry its full always-on topology forward by default based on current evidence.

nextEvidence: Run only a small number of additional high-risk repetitions/tasks to estimate how often peer escalation adds unique value; do not resume broad topology sweeps.
Define deterministic high-risk/escalation predicates in product policy.
Productize report/validation/credential integrity invariants from issue #8 in the normal tool/session boundary.
Then validate the adaptive route policy end-to-end before replacing released v0.2 orchestration.
